questions.problem:
For the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x,y)=x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+y\operatorname{sin}⁡x,
$$

the quadratic Taylor polynomial of $f$ about $a=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
f(x,y)≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{1}{2}{[\begin{aligned}∗ \\ y\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & ∗\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}∗ \\ y\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the sum of the three missing expressions.
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose that the function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶z
$$

 

and is twice differentiable at $x=a.$ Then, the quadratic Taylor polynomial of $f$ about $a$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{1}{2}(x-a)^{T}{f}^{″}(a)(x-a),\end{aligned}
$$

where

$$
{f}^{′}(a)={[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]|}_{x=a}
$$

and

$$
{f}^{″}(a)={[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}]}_{x=a}
$$

In this case, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}], & \,{f}^{″}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Calculating the first derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡y+y\operatorname{cos}⁡x & \operatorname{sin}⁡x-x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Calculating the second derivative, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}-y\operatorname{sin}⁡x & \operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡y \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡y & -x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\end{aligned}] \\ {f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{2},0) & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{\pi }{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the second-degree Taylor polynomial is given by

$$
f(x)≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{1}{2}{[\begin{aligned}x-\frac{\pi }{2} \\ y\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{\pi }{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x-\frac{\pi }{2} \\ y\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the sum of the missing expressions is

$$
(x-\frac{\pi }{2})+(-\frac{\pi }{2})+(x-\frac{\pi }{2})=2x-\frac{3\pi }{2}.
$$

questions.problem:
For the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x,y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-y),
$$

the quadratic Taylor polynomial of $f$ about $a=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈∗+[\begin{aligned}∗ & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}∗ \\ y\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}{[\begin{aligned}∗ \\ y\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}∗ & 3 \\ ∗ & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the sum of the six missing expressions.
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose that the function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is defened by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶z
$$

 

and is twice differentiable at $x=a.$ Then, the quadratic Taylor polynomial of $f$ about $a$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{1}{2}(x-a)^{T}{f}^{″}(a)(x-a),\end{aligned}
$$

where

$$
{f}^{′}(a)={[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]|}_{x=a}
$$

and

$$
{f}^{″}(a)={[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}]}_{x=a}
$$

In this case, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}], & \,{f}^{″}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the terms of our Taylor polynomial:

- Calculating the value of the function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0,0) & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

- Calculating the first derivatives, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-y) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-y)\end{aligned}] \\ {f}^{′}(0,0) & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- Calculating the second derivative, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}-9\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-y) & 3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-y) \\ 3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-y) & -\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-y)\end{aligned}] \\ {f}^{″}(0,0) & =[\begin{aligned}-9 & 3 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the second-degree Taylor polynomial is given by

$$
f(x)≈1+[\begin{aligned}0 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}{[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}-9 & 3 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, the sum of the missing expressions is

$$
1+0+x+x+(-9)+3=2x-5.
$$

questions.problem:
For the twice-differentiable function $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ we have the following data:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1,0) & =3, & \,{f}^{′}(1,0) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}], & \,{f}^{″}(1,0) & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Use the quadratic Taylor polynomial of $f$ about $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ to approximate the value of $f(1,2).$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose that the function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶z
$$

 

and is twice differentiable at $x=a.$ Then, the quadratic Taylor polynomial of $f$ about $a$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{1}{2}(x-a)^{T}{f}^{″}(a)(x-a),\end{aligned}
$$

where

$$
{f}^{′}(a)={[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]|}_{x=a}
$$

and

$$
{f}^{″}(a)={[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}]}_{x=a}
$$

In this case, we have $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],$ and the following data:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(a) & =3, & \,{f}^{′}(a) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}], & \,{f}^{″}(a) & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the second-degree Taylor polynomial is given by

$$
f(x)≈3+[\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x-1 \\ y\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}{[\begin{aligned}x-1 \\ y\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x-1 \\ y\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, evaluating the polynomial at $x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1,2) & ≈3+[\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}{[\begin{aligned}1-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =3+[\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =3+(-2)+\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =1+\frac{1}{2}(4) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1,1) & =2, & \,{f}^{′}(1,1) & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1\end{aligned}], & \,{f}^{″}(1,1) & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

questions.worked_solution:
Suppose that the function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶z
$$

 

and is twice differentiable at $x=a.$ Then, the quadratic Taylor polynomial of $f$ about $a$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{1}{2}(x-a)^{T}{f}^{″}(a)(x-a),\end{aligned}
$$

where

$$
{f}^{′}(a)={[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]|}_{x=a}
$$

and

$$
{f}^{″}(a)={[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}]}_{x=a}
$$

In this case, we have $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ and the following data:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(a) & =2, & \,{f}^{′}(a) & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1\end{aligned}], & \,{f}^{″}(a) & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the second-degree Taylor polynomial is given by

$$
f(x)≈2+[\begin{aligned}3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x-1 \\ y-1\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}{[\begin{aligned}x-1 \\ y-1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x-1 \\ y-1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, evaluating the polynomial at $x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0,2) & ≈2+[\begin{aligned}3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0-1 \\ 2-1\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}{[\begin{aligned}0-1 \\ 2-1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0-1 \\ 2-1\end{aligned}] \\  & =2+[\begin{aligned}3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =2+(-2)+\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =0+\frac{1}{2}(0) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Suppose that the function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶z
$$

 

and is twice differentiable at $x=a.$ Then, the quadratic Taylor polynomial of $f$ about $a$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{1}{2}(x-a)^{T}{f}^{″}(a)(x-a),\end{aligned}
$$

where

$$
{f}^{′}(a)={[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]|}_{x=a}
$$

and

$$
{f}^{″}(a)={[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}]}_{x=a}
$$

In this case, we have $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],$ and the following data:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(a) & =1+e, & \,{f}^{′}(a) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}], & \,{f}^{″}(a) & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the second-degree Taylor polynomial is given by

$$
f(x)≈1+e+[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x-1 \\ y-1 \\ z\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}{[\begin{aligned}x-1 \\ y-1 \\ z\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x-1 \\ y-1 \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, evaluating the polynomial at $x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2,2,2) & ≈1+e+[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2-1 \\ 2-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}{[\begin{aligned}2-1 \\ 2-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2-1 \\ 2-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =1+e+[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =1+e+6+\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =7+e+\frac{1}{2}(14) \\  & =14+e.\end{aligned}
$$
